claims.text: The driver's own trace shows he held position inside the pickup geofence for only 179 seconds, one second short of the 180-second free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip, so the required dwell under POL-NS-01(c) was never served and the fee is not chargeable.

The shortfall is stated arithmetically by the trace itself: the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 179 seconds against a minimum dwell of 180 seconds for STANDARD, a shortfall of 1.0 second, and POL-NS-06 makes that shortfall a full refund of the cancellation fee whether or not the rider was present.

The trip record confirms the same clock: the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 22:38:39 and the driver cancelled at 22:41:36, three minutes later, so the driver terminated the trip at the very moment the waiting period elapsed rather than after it, and the cancellation cannot fall at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed under POL-NS-01(d).

The rider's device was stationary throughout the waiting window at a mean distance of about 899 m from the pickup pin, with a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph across 53 fixes, so the rider was not moving away and the driver's own account that he 'waited the free period then cancelled' is not corroborated by any rider-side flight.

The driver's only chat message, 'im at the pickup point', was sent at 22:38:57 and read at 22:39:27, and the driver cancelled at 22:41:36 without any further message or in-app call, so the driver had the rider's attention and still terminated the trip one second before the waiting period he was owed had run.

The fare ledger shows the full $4.50 cancellation fee was charged and remains CHARGED with no refund issued, so the contested amount is live and a full refund of the cancellation-fee line is the remedy the shortfall clause directs.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road in this window - the advisory artifact is MISSING with a BLOCKING issue - so the driver cannot accumulate dwell across separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i), and the 179-second run stands as the whole of the dwell.

The driver's profile shows 2 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 91 completed trips, a rate of about 0.022, which is below the 0.08 anti-farming threshold, so the fee is not withheld on that ground and the shortfall refund is not displaced by POL-NS-07.

claims.text: The trip record shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:38:37 and the platform's own wait timer started two seconds later at 22:38:39, so the arrival event required by POL-NS-01(a) exists on the record.

The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 179 seconds, from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, on 19 qualifying fixes — so POL-NS-01(b) is satisfied on the driver's track, not merely on his button press.

The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and the driver's in-geofence dwell measured from the first qualifying fix is 179 seconds — a shortfall of exactly 1 second against the minimum dwell for STANDARD. I concede this point: on the arithmetic the dwell does not reach the required minimum, and POL-NS-06 therefore refunds the cancellation fee in full.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: the driver's trace shows him stationary at the pin (min_distance_m 0.31 m) at the arrival timestamp, not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or more, so the waiting clock runs from the arrival event and is not recomputed. The 1-second shortfall is therefore a genuine shortfall, not an artefact of a false marker.

The driver did attempt to coordinate: he sent an in-app message at 22:38:57 reading 'im at the pickup point', which the rider read at 22:39:27. That is a driver-side locating message during the waiting window, and it is inconsistent with the rider's claim that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately'.

The rider's own track places her device roughly 895 to 903 m from the pickup pin throughout the window (mean_distance_m 898.93 m), far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and she recorded zero qualifying fixes inside that radius. She was not at the pickup point when the driver waited there.

The rider's claim that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the record: the driver was en route from 22:30:27, arrived at 22:38:37, and cancelled at 22:41:36 — three minutes of waiting after arrival, on a trip whose optimal duration was 41.1 minutes. The cancellation was not immediate.

The fare ledger reconciles: the cancellation fee charged is SGD 4.50, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, so the amount in dispute is the correct figure and the only question is whether it was chargeable at all.

The driver's anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2/91 is 0.022, below the 0.08 rate. His profile therefore does not bar compensation on its own terms — though on this record the 1-second dwell shortfall means POL-NS-07 is not reached at all.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road: EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be used to accumulate separate in-geofence intervals or to excuse the shortfall. The absence is citable but it does not help the driver here — it removes the only route by which the 1-second gap could have been bridged.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so neither the POL-NS-09(d) abuse trigger nor the POL-NS-09(c) repeat-pairing trigger fires. Nothing in the profiles escalates this case, and nothing in them may ground an adverse finding against the rider under POL-GEN-01.

The GPS trace is clean: 100.0% coverage, 74 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so no POL-NS-08(b) trace defect arises and the 179-second dwell measurement is reliable. The shortfall is real, not an artefact of a gapped or sparse trace.

ruling.explanation: Both parties, this one turns on a single second. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:38:37 on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02717), and his GPS trace (EV-GPS-02717) shows one continuous qualifying run inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, from 22:38:37 to the 22:41:36 cancellation — 179 seconds on 19 qualifying fixes. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap. The dwell is therefore 1 second short: limb (c) is not met, and the cancellation at 22:41:36 did not fall at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, so limb (d) fails too. POL-NS-06 is strict: a shortfall in the waiting period refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present. That is why the driver's evidence that the rider's own device sat about 899 m from the pin (EV-GPS-02717, rider_track) does not save the fee — it is accepted, but POL-NS-06 does not read rider presence, and there is no rider-side flight to corroborate. The arrival marker is genuine and not false: at the arrival timestamp the driver was stationary at the pin (minimum distance 0.31 m) and not moving at 15 km/h or more, so POL-NS-05 does not fire and no false-arrival referral arises. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02717) reconciles to the platform figure — $4.50 net — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the $4.50 is the correct amount to return. No escalation trigger fires: no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the anti-farming check on POL-NS-07 does not trip (2 no-show terminations against 91 completed trips, about 2.2%, below the 4-count and 0.08-rate limbs); and the profiles show no repeat-pairing or abuse pattern. Driver compensation is not reached at all, because POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full with no compensation payable. All artifacts relied on carry weight 1.0, so no POL-GEN-02(3) discount applies; the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02717-01, weight 0.0) carries nothing here and its two citing claims were properly discarded for not naming the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code. Outcome: the $4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider; the monetary effect of $4.50 is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue. Both parties retain the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 is refunded to the rider in full. No driver compensation is payable.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. Driver DRV-09717 accepted the booking at 22:30:19 and reached the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 pickup at 22:38:37, tapping 'I'm Here' (EV-TRIP-02717). He cancelled at 22:41:36 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02717) places his vehicle inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, across 19 qualifying fixes, a continuous in-geofence run of 179 seconds. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02717) shows the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line charged, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The rider's own device track (EV-GPS-02717) sits about 899 m from the pin throughout, and the only chat message is the driver's 'im at the pickup point' sent 22:38:57 and read 22:39:27 (EV-CHAT-02717).

THE DECIDING ARITHMETIC. POL-NS-01 lets this fee stand only if all four of its limbs hold. Limb (a) holds (the 'arrived' event exists, 22:38:37) and limb (b) holds (the driver's qualifying fixes are inside the arrival radius). Limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period in force, and that period is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, EV-TRIP-02717). The measured dwell is 179 seconds (EV-GPS-02717 derived longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec), a shortfall of 1.0 second. Limb (d) fails with it, because the 22:41:36 cancellation did not fall at or after the moment the required 180-second dwell elapsed. POL-NS-06 then governs on its own terms: where the effective dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. This is strict by design - the waiting period is the consideration the fee was paid for - so a one-second shortfall is a full refund, not a partial one. Both advocates reached this result, the Driver Advocate expressly conceding the shortfall.

CLAIMS ANSWERED. Driver claims that POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied are accepted on the evidence, but they do not carry the clause: limb (c) fails, so the conjunctive test in POL-NS-01 is not met and the fee is not chargeable. The Driver Advocate's concession that the 179-second dwell falls one second short of the 180-second minimum is accepted, and it is the ground of decision. The driver's POL-NS-05 claim is accepted: his minimum distance to the pin at the arrival timestamp is 0.31 m and he was stationary, so the arrival marker is not false and the waiting clock is not recomputed - the 1-second shortfall is a genuine shortfall and not an artefact of an early tap. The driver's POL-NS-08(d) reconciliation claim is accepted: the charged line of SGD 4.50 matches platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50, so no fare defect arises and the disputed amount is the correct figure. The driver's claim that the rider was roughly 899 m from the pickup is accepted (EV-GPS-02717 rider_track, mean 898.93 m against a 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius), but it does not change the outcome: POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider here because the only chat message is the driver's, not hers, and in any event POL-NS-06 refunds on the shortfall alone irrespective of rider presence. The driver's claim that the rider's account of an 'almost immediate' cancellation is contradicted by the record is accepted - three minutes elapsed between arrival and cancellation on a trip whose optimal duration was 41.1 minutes - but that finding does not defeat the refund, because the fee is not chargeable once the dwell falls short. The Rider Advocate's claims on the 179-second run, the 1.0-second shortfall, the 22:38:39 wait timer and the 22:41:36 cancellation are accepted and are the same arithmetic this ruling rests on. The claim that the driver cancelled 'at the very moment the waiting period elapsed rather than after it' is accepted: on the platform's own timer (22:38:39 to 22:41:36) and on the GPS-measured dwell (179 seconds), the termination preceded the elapse of the 180-second period, so limb (d) fails as well as limb (c). The fare-ledger claim that the SGD 4.50 line is live and unrefunded is accepted.

PROFILES. The two anti-farming claims cite only driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d (2) and driver_profile.completed_trips_30d (91), and the escalation claims cite only rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d (0) and the two disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields (0) - all fields POL-GEN-01 makes citable for those tests. Those claims are accepted: 2 is below the POL-NS-07 threshold of 4, 2/91 is 0.022, below the 0.08 rate, and neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) fires. No other profile field was used as a ground for or against either party, and no adverse finding rests on reputation.

INTEGRITY AND ESCALATION. No limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged. There is no clock skew under limb (a): the 'arrived' event at 22:38:37 matches the nearest GPS fix at 22:38:37. There is no trace defect under limb (b): coverage is 100.0%, 74 fixes at a 10-second cadence, max_gap_sec 0.0, and the rider_track is present. There is no chat defect under limb (c): one message logged against trip_record.chat_message_count of 1, with no missing sequence number. There is no fare defect under limb (d), as the ledger reconciles. POL-NS-09 is therefore not triggered: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, the repeat-pairing and abuse triggers are at zero, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no deciding fact rests on an impaired artifact. No escalation, and no referral, is warranted. Both of you agree on the arithmetic, and so do I. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:38:37 and cancelled at 22:41:36. Measured the way POL-NS-01(c) requires — from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix (EV-GPS-02717, longest qualifying run first_ts 22:38:37, last_ts 22:41:36, duration_sec 179.0), not from the button press — the driver held position inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for 179 seconds. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (EV-TRIP-02717, platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so the dwell falls short by 1.0 second (derived.arrival.shortfall_sec 1.0). The platform's own wait timer tells the same story from the other end: it started at 22:38:39 and would not have expired until 22:41:39, three seconds after the 22:41:36 cancellation.

This is not an artefact of a false arrival marker. The driver's trace shows him stationary at the pin (min_distance_m 0.31 m) at the arrival timestamp, so POL-NS-05 does not fire, the waiting clock is not recomputed, and the 179-second figure is the genuine dwell. The arrival event required by POL-NS-01(a) exists, and limb (b) is satisfied on the driver's own track. But limb (c) requires the full free waiting period, and it was not served. Limb (d) likewise requires the cancellation to fall at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed; it fell one second before.

Under POL-NS-06 the consequence is not discretionary: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The rider is therefore refunded the whole cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-02717, cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). No driver compensation is payable under POL-NS-06, so driver_compensation_sgd is null.

On the driver's side I record two things in his favour, though neither changes the outcome. First, the rider's claim that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is not accurate on the raw record: the driver was en route from 22:30:27, arrived at 22:38:37 and waited roughly three minutes before cancelling on a trip of about 41 minutes. Second, the driver did try to coordinate — his 22:38:57 in-app message 'im at the pickup point' was read at 22:39:27. But POL-NS-06 is strict liability precisely so that a rider who was genuinely absent still recovers the fee when the waiting period the fee buys was not served in full, and the rider's own track (roughly 899 m from the pin throughout) does not change that. Because the fee is not chargeable, the driver's payout under POL-NS-07 is never reached; in any event the anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 2, below 4; 2/91 ≈ 0.022, below 0.08).

No context-only profile field grounds any finding (POL-GEN-01).

The deciding fact — a 179-second dwell against a 180-second requirement — is carried by EV-GPS-02717 and EV-TRIP-02717, both at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is set at 0.90, above the 0.70 floor, and no trigger in POL-NS-09(a) to (e) fires, so the case is not escalated. No referral is produced: the arrival marker was not false, so POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire; RIDER_NO_SHOW is a recognised limb (d) reason code, so no mis-selection referral arises; and no other clause adds an instruction.
